records.selected_section: Rotation strategy: single user and alternating users
records.supported: For the documented database single-user strategy, existing connections are not dropped; new authentication can face a short change/update interval. Alternating users has its own permission/propagation conditions.
records.application: Do not claim that single-user rotation universally drops connections or that any temporary interruption itself violates every service contract. Bind observed interruption, controlled recovery, actual agreed window and truthful completion.
records.limitations: Apply the documented strategy only to its supported engine, connection and recovery conditions.

records.selected_section: Container hooks, Hook handler execution and delivery guarantees
records.supported: PostStart is concurrent with entrypoint. PreStop and normal stop share the grace period; hooks may be redelivered, not arbitrarily retried on every failure.
records.version_scope: rolling docs showingv1.37 navigation, selected current text observed2026-10-23; not an installed cluster version
records.application: The shared budget is a technical precondition; mere expiration and force termination does not prove accepted business work was lost.
records.limitations: Apply the documented strategy only to its supported engine, connection and recovery conditions.

records.selected_section: Pod Termination Flow and Forced Pod termination
records.supported: The documented flow can request a small extension for an outstanding PreStop and forcibly stop remaining processes at expiration. Immediate API removal does not prove the process stopped.
records.application: A lawful forced stop after accounted work remains possible; completion and durable recovery observations, not the signal alone, determine the bounded request-accounting predicate.
records.limitations: Apply the documented strategy only to its supported engine, connection and recovery conditions.

records.selected_section: Overview of Oracle RAC and architecture/processing
records.supported: RAC explicitly coordinates multiple instances accessing one shared database with supported cluster-aware storage and cache/resource coordination.
records.version_scope: Oracle26 RAC introduction and architecture overview
records.application: Shared storage or multiple physical writers is not universally an error. Require a supported, validated coordination/authority contract; this does not recommend, license or certify RAC, generic NFS or any container deployment.
records.limitations: Apply the documented strategy only to its supported engine, connection and recovery conditions.

records.selected_section: Shared Disk Failover; Logical Replication; asynchronous/synchronous multimaster
records.supported: The guide distinguishes single-active shared-disk failover from multidirectional logical or middleware/multimaster designs. Its shared-disk standby exclusion is architecture-specific; PostgreSQL does not natively offer the discussed synchronous multimaster mode.
records.application: Do not extend a single-primary fencing example into a ban on every supported multiwriter architecture. Single-primary scopes still reject old writers; other modes need explicit supported coordination/conflict and business invariants.
records.limitations: Apply the documented strategy only to its supported engine, connection and recovery conditions.
